absent: Locking discipline, concurrency and interrupt safety for the exercised bitmap, bitops and BPF helpers.
Exported symbols or module load and unload wiring beyond the static test routines shown.
Engine that executes BPF test programs and compares results, including verifier and JIT interaction.
State machine for test progression, subtest selection and failure reporting.
Deallocation and lifetime rules for dynamically built maximum-size programs.

findings.text: Narrow bitmap access tolerates degenerate widths against a null map without crashing; zero width and wider than word width are exercised as safe cases while the read result there is treated as undefined.

A narrow write followed by a read at the same offset preserves the value, and two adjacent narrow writes merge into one wider read with the expected combined asymmetric pattern across a sliding start offset.

Zero-length bitmap mutation, query, conversion, shift and find operations accept null maps and zero counts as safe calls, covering set, clear, fill, zero, copy, logic, weight, subset, array conversion and the find families.

Boot-time bitmap self-check runs a fixed sequence of functional subtests for clear, fill, copy, region, replace, scatter, array conversion, parsing, printing, optimisation, cut, constant evaluation, narrow access, performance, weight and iterator helpers.
Bit-operation self-test uses probe positions 4, 7, 11, 31 and 88 with a sentinel value 255 and a bitmap length 256.
Order helpers are checked against known input to expected-order pairs including small values near powers of two and large 32-bit and 64-bit edge values with expected results up to 31, 32, 63 and 64.
The find-nth-set helper is exercised for every shift width over a large random buffer with the whole sweep timed and logged; allocation failure aborts with an out-of-memory status.

Bitops startup sets the probe bits, validates count-order helpers against the tables including the 64-bit table on 64-bit builds, enforces ordering, clears the probes, verifies that no bit remains set, runs the helper sweep and logs completion.
Performance and degenerate-width paths use volatile sinks and once-accessors plus an ordering barrier so the compiler cannot fold away or reorder the measured bitmap, bitops and find operations.
BPF self-test limits are 3 subtests per case, 1000 default runs, 128 bytes of packet and fragment data, 512 embedded instructions, and a maximum immediate value with all 32 bits set.
Synthetic packet metadata uses type 3, mark 0x1234aaaa, hash 0x1234aaab, queue 123, VLAN tag with all bits set and present flag 1, device index 577 and device type 588.
Test shorthand names R0 through R10 alias the extended registers in order through the frame pointer.

Each BPF case carries a description, a union holding classic, extended or externally allocated program storage, a flag byte, input bytes, per-subtest size and expected result, an optional program builder callback, an expected error, fragment bytes, a stack depth and an optional run count.

Case flags occupy low bits for no-data, expected failure, fragment input, verifier zero-extension and large memory, while two higher bits select classic versus extended instruction sets combined by a type mask.

Maximum-size program builders allocate a full-length instruction buffer, fill it with a characteristic pattern such as constant returns, chained arithmetic, jumps, absolute loads or header loads, publish pointer and length in the case object, and report allocation failure.

Jump-stress builder tiles unconditional jumps in fixed-size blocks with a computed tail plus a terminal return, reused by small and maximum-size cases to exercise multi-pass branch resolution and padding.

Atomic-store stress builder emits an initial move and store followed by a long run of atomic adds at one stack slot and a final load and exit, recording a stack depth of 40; word and double-word widths share one parametrised helper.

Maximum-displacement jump harness builds a wide immediate load plus a conditional branch at the largest signed 16-bit offset followed by fall-through, exit and long arithmetic filler ending in exit, with taken, not-taken, always-taken and never-taken variants in 32-bit and 64-bit forms.

Reference arithmetic helper emulates move, logic, shifts including arithmetic sign fill, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and modulo with 32-bit narrowing and signed handling, signalling failure on zero divisor and on the signed minimum-divisor edge handled elsewhere.
Both bitops and BPF self-test modules prefix log output with the module name.
Read and write microbenchmarks sweep every width from one to word size over every valid offset several times while pinning results through volatile or once stores and reporting elapsed time.
